pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: src/stores/reviewStore.ts:597 When the SLA expires, the 'escalate' rung only stamps escalatedAt on the in-memory row. parseManualReview resets it to null on the next 15 s fetch (reviewStore.ts:103), and nothing renders it, so no other person ever receives the item, and the critical and warning rungs act as an unrecorded, silent hold.

techniques.evidence: src/stores/reviewStore.ts:597 The ladder is one table (review-sla.ts:41) with a closed three-member action set that includes 'none' (hold). But 'escalate' pushes at no different human and records nothing durable; it is wiped by the refetch at reviewStore.ts:103.

src/lib/review-sla.ts:207 The check runs at load and throws a message that names the consequence, which is good. But it permits equality, as does the stored-policy validator at review-sla.ts:187. The standard calls equality a zero-width window and a violation. It also compares only against the ramp's start, not its 3x end.

src/stores/reviewStore.ts:61 An unparseable payload or invalid severity defaults to critical and sets parseError. The marker shows on the row (ReviewRow.tsx:246) and as a role=alert in the detail panel (ReviewDetailPanel.tsx:115). An unreadable timestamp is treated as due now (review-sla.ts:73).

src/hooks/useReviewBulkActions.ts:91 'Select all' takes every pending row in the status filter, across mixed severities and personas, and bulk approve needs no confirmation. That is the heterogeneous sweep the technique says should be absent. Positives: the badge derives from the same overlay (countPending), and a failed write keeps the item and reselects it.

src/stores/reviewStore.ts:429 The verdict carries the literal sentinel 'You' (review-display.ts:10), not an authenticated decider. No content version or fingerprint is bound, and nothing records what was shown.
